questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area ahead.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn left only after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Turn left because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left only after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians first.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:

options.text: Keep going through the intersection.
Stop right away.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive through carefully.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive through carefully.
questions.explanation: When the light turns yellow, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if it is safe. If you cannot stop safely, drive through the intersection carefully.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing the intersection.
Always stop completely at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. You must slow down and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if necessary.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop signs or traffic lights, you should:

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed.
Stop, look both ways, then go.
Let all other drivers go first.
Be ready to yield to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to other drivers.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, be ready to yield. Watch for vehicles coming from the right. Slow down and be prepared to stop to avoid a crash.

questions.question: Your blood alcohol content (BAC) does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much alcohol you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, when you drink, and your body weight. It does not depend on how fit you are or how well you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: If you move to a new address, you must tell the Department of Licensing:

options.text: Within 10 days.
Within 30 days.
At your next license renewal.
When your license no longer matches your checkbook.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 10 days.
questions.explanation: You must notify the Department of Licensing within 10 days of moving or changing your legal name.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires pointing straight ahead.
Turn the steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn the steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking facing uphill, turn the wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will hit the curb and stop.

questions.question: Your turn signal must be on for at least how long before you change direction?

options.text: 50 feet.
75 feet.
100 feet.
125 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet.
questions.explanation: Signal for at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycles?

options.text: Other drivers can follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with one rider.
You must move your car completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
You can expect to see a motorcycle's brake lights when it slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move your car completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane of space. Make sure your car is completely in the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause your engine to use too much oil.
Mean your vehicle needs a tune-up sooner than usual.
Make you feel sleepy while driving.
Start fires in grass on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from the engine and cools hot gases. A leaky exhaust system can be deadly. The fumes can also make you drowsy while driving.

questions.question: What is a "No zone?"

options.text: A marked no-passing zone
A one-way traffic area
The blind spot around a large vehicle
An area for motor vehicles only

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot around a large vehicle
questions.explanation: "No zones" are large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Drivers of smaller cars should not stay in these blind spots.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb:

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels toward the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle downhill on a two-way street:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the right edge of the road. If your vehicle rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must not pass another vehicle.
You may pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You may pass if you know the road ahead is clear.
You may pass, but only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must not pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white rectangles with black markings. Drivers must follow all instructions on regulatory signs. This sign means passing is not allowed.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: Round signs indicate:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Upcoming railroad crossings.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you of an upcoming railroad crossing. Be extra careful near railroad crossings.

questions.question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and you may pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction and you may pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means passing is not allowed.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. You should:

options.text: Move slowly until the traffic ahead clears.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can go all the way through.
Use your horn to make cars move ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can go all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive all the way through. Wait until the traffic ahead moves so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: Drivers under 21 cannot drive if they have any THC in their blood. At minimum, drivers 21 and older cannot drive with more than ____ nanograms of THC per milliliter of blood.

options.text: Zero nanograms
One nanogram
Three nanograms
Five nanograms

questions.correctAnswerText: Zero nanograms
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot have any THC in their blood. Drivers 21 and older cannot drive with more than five nanograms of THC per milliliter of blood. Marijuana use while driving is very dangerous.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road angles toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will be required to turn left just ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the edge of the road shows where the road ends. It marks the boundary between the driving lane and the shoulder. When this line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: When do roads become most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. This is worse in hot weather, when heat and water cause more oil to rise to the surface.

questions.question: Your vehicle takes longer to stop when you are driving on:

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distances are longer on wet or icy roads. Stopping distances also increase on roads with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: You are backing out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do before moving?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children that you are moving.
Sound your horn so the children will hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Look through your back window for people and obstacles. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are nearby. Get out and check the area behind your vehicle before backing out of a driveway.
